newsitem.title: USA: Merck delays AIDS drug distribution - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Merck delays AIDS drug distribution - WSJ.

text.p: Merck & Co will postpone until next year its plans to expand the distribution of its new AIDS drug to retail pharmacies because its production facilities cannot keep up with demand, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

The newspaper said a company spokesman said Merck had decided to expand distribution "more broadly sometime next year" as its new factories gradually produce greater quantities of the drug, known as Crixivan.
It said the company had not been able to build enough inventory to start distributing the drug.
The drug is one of three protease drugs that can greatly reduce levels of the AIDS virus in a patient's blood when mixed with other drugs.
The United States approved Crixivan in March and other countries were also quickly approving the drug, the newspaper said.
